title: Attachment ordinary failures and recovery

install.basis: real candidate source checkout in its repository virtual environment

terminal.program: Talaria via POSIX PTY on macOS

actions:
Missing-file and permission-denied attempts show nothing was sent; unsupported PDF shows the explicit client format exclusion. No attach request or prompt submission occurs for those refusal actions; their later corrected file produces one prompt.submit and the actual fixture answer in the same conversation.
Oversize image.attach_bytes returns gateway4018: image too large (28830054 bytes; cap25MB). The visible notice names the size cap and shrink-and-retry action. Corrected attachment recovery completes in the same conversation.
The image-incapable route is transport-inapplicable: this gateway routes images to auxiliary vision even when the acting model lacks image support; Talaria has no client-visible capability flag to induce this route. This rests on the architectural ruling alone, not a claimed4016 capture.
The test-only client link drops the first file.attach before forwarding it. Talaria retains the command and displays interruption plus uncertain staging after reconnect. Retry produces the actual attached-file answer; Hermes itself is not restarted.
Jeff authorized gemini-3.6-flash through gemini for the unreadable, unsupported and oversize recovery sessions, each selected with --session. Missing-file and transfer recovery used the original muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free actor. Gateway, credentials, profile, shared default and tester model/account were unchanged.

actual:

Each complete wire interval has exactly one prompt.submit for its successful recovery. Jeff authorized gemini-3.6-flash through gemini for the unreadable, unsupported and oversize recovery sessions, each selected with --session. This rests on the architectural ruling alone, not a claimed4016 capture. (https://github.com/infiquetra/talaria/issues/147); The case explicitly allows a documented transport-inapplicable disposition; auxiliary vision routing is gateway-controlled and no client flag induces incapability.
